script: I lied about prescriptions—my husband caught me, and the truth stunned everyone.. I am 32, he's 36, and we've been together almost 13 years. I've always been a hot mess with my mental health—therapy, self‑talk, you name it. A few years back I told my husband I was thinking about getting prescription meds. He blew up, said it was a bad idea, and I just swallowed the punch. Fast forward to now. I am 32, still juggling anxiety, and I finally decided I needed help. I got an anti‑anxiety/antidepressant prescription and didn't tell him. Two months later, I am actually feeling better. I was supposed to wait until I knew it worked before spilling the tea, but every time I tried, I'd freeze, thinking he'd be upset, that he'd love me less, that I'd lose his trust. I am a coward, yes. Last night, I set my anxiety pill on the counter, planned to take it after my bedtime routine. I forgot. I went to bed. He found it in the morning. I was half‑asleep when he asked. "Pain reliever," I blurted out. Another epic fail. Within ten minutes I broke down and told him the whole truth. He's furious. He says he can't trust me if I can hide something like that every day. I never thought a pill would make him question my trustworthiness. I am ashamed. I love him, crave his respect, and I just ruined it. He's gone to work. I am left staring at the ceiling, thinking, "What the heck is wrong with me? How did I let this happen?" I am terrified I've destroyed our relationship. I am the only one I can blame. I didn't give him enough credit before. He's sweet, caring. His mom's issues with prescription meds probably fed the stigma. This all just happened, and I am hoping tomorrow we can have a better conversation. I am scared, but I know I have to own this.
